chunks: And the Sheikh — may God support him — informed me, saying: Abu al-Qasim Ja'far ibn Muhammad ibn Qulawayh informed me, from Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan and Ahmad ibn Idris, from Muhammad ibn Abd al-Jabbar — all of them — from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Salim Abu al-Fadl, from Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), who said:
Nothing nullifies the wudu except what exits from your two lower extremities, the two which God has blessed you with.

key_terms.أَنْعَمَ اللَّهُ بِهِمَا عَلَيْكَ: God has blessed you with them both — theologically grounding the ruling in divine creation and grace
key_terms.الْوُضُوءَ: wudu — ritual ablution required before salat and other acts of worship
key_terms.طَرَفَيْكَ الْأَسْفَلَيْنِ: your two lower extremities — Imamic euphemism for the urethra and anus, the two lower bodily orifices
key_terms.يَنْقُضُ: nullifies/breaks — the technical fiqh term for invalidating wudu

ai.seo_question: What are the acts that nullify wudu according to Imam al-Sadiq (AS) in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) issues a precise legal ruling confining the nullifiers of wudu exclusively to discharges from the two lower bodily orifices (the urethra and anus), employing a theologically charged euphemism — 'the two which God has blessed you with' — to acknowledge divine grace while establishing a strict limiting principle. This ruling is foundational in Shia fiqh: it excludes acts such as sleep, bleeding, vomiting, or touching that other legal traditions count as nullifiers, grounding the rule in the physical reality of the body as God-given.
word_analysis: with them both / by means of them (dual)
